name: Citizenship by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: Anyone born inside or outside Syria to a Syrian Arab father acquires Syrian nationality automatically (Article 3(A), reinforced by Article 30: 'children shall have the nationality of the father').

Article 3(B) permits acquisition only when the child is born IN Syria to a Syrian Arab mother AND the father is unknown -- a narrow exception, not a general right of mothers to transmit nationality the way fathers can.

sources.title: MENA Rights Group -- hosted English translation of Syria's Nationality Act (Legislative Decree No. 276 of 1969): Articles 3, 30 governing descent-based acquisition

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Syria). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to a human-rights NGO's hosted translation of the primary legal text (tier 2), not a Syrian government portal directly, so a hard requirement citing it cannot support 'published' status under this dataset's rules even though the underlying law itself is a real, current government-enacted statute. STARK GENDER ASYMMETRY, WORSE THAN MOST COUNTRIES BUILT IN THIS DATASET: a Syrian father transmits nationality unconditionally to his children born anywhere in the world; a Syrian mother can only transmit it if the birth occurs INSIDE Syria AND the father is unknown -- there is no general maternal-descent right at all, not even a reduced or conditional one, unlike Kuwait's narrow-but-real maternal exception or Kazakhstan/Tanzania's full gender-neutral descent rules built elsewhere in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed set null: no explicit renunciation or dual-citizenship clause was found in the sections of the 1969 Act reviewed for this build; this is disclosed as unconfirmed, not asserted as permitted. This Act predates the December 2024 change of government -- whether and how it continues to be applied by the transitional administration was not independently confirmed in this build.
